contrary_evidence: Poland reported continued electricity supply after the destructive December 2025 attempts; cyber access and attempted harm do not establish national blackout.
Reuters reports on 2 November 2026 did not establish a perpetrator or forensic linkage among national supermarket refrigeration incidents.
ENISA and CERT-EU use defined, nonrepresentative incident universes; their percentages cannot be added or converted into global attack probabilities.
Mandiant finds most observed successful intrusions still exploited human and systemic weaknesses, despite new AI-enabled attack workflows.
EEAS FIMI incident/channel counts do not show that voters changed their behavior or that an election outcome was altered.
limitations: Same-day November 2 reports are provisional; attribution, store counts, financial losses and technical linkage require independent forensic revision.
Source incident data and vendor investigations are selected observational samples with distinct denominators and disclosure biases.
Russian, Chinese and other official attributions are identified as institutional statements, not blanket proofs across unrelated incidents.
Forward scenarios for 2027–2030 are conditional and have no defensible precise probability.
A prior general Marginal Thinking cyberwarfare-and-AI study exists; this research focuses on new civilian, economic, psychological and European incident dynamics.
scenarios: Bounded recurring disruption with short restoration
Cyber-physical escalation linked to geopolitical crisis
Greater civilian infrastructure resilience and measured recoverability

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 2 November 2026; Reuters day-of reports, September 2026 ENISA, October 2026 CERT-EU, 2026 IMF/GTIG/Microsoft/Mandiant/Council/Poland statements; observations and release dates distinguished.
producer_checks.editorial_novelty: Separate from the 21 October theoretical cyberwarfare-and-AI article; forensic European retail incidents, economics of civilian OT, supply-chain concentration, psychosocial harms, finance and observable scenarios.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Each locale contains three matching evidence/comparison tables, two comparable numeric bar charts, one causal flow and one geographic regional exposure map.
producer_checks.source_check: 23 matched official/specialist/news URLs, including Reuters, ENISA, CERT-EU, Polish government/CERT Polska, EU Council, Google/Mandiant, Microsoft, IMF, EEAS and ICRC.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: English 4016 substantive words and PT-BR 3986; 16 substantive numbered sections, 23 matching URLs, matching two chart data series, equivalent table/flow/map semantics.
producer_checks.methodology: Separate intrusion from sabotage, state nexus from unknown actor, official allegation from technical proof, observed 2025 annual sample from 2 November 2026 incident reporting, and physical effect from macroeconomic scenario.

en.title: Cyber conflict as a system of power: Europe’s new attacks, global digital coercion and the economics of civilian vulnerability
en.deck: A deep historical, political-economic and psychological study of cyber conflict through 2 November 2026: European retail refrigeration, Polish energy sabotage, government and medical breaches, Russia–EU coercion, global competition, AI, law, civilian harm and five falsifiable futures.
en.regime: Chronic below-threshold digital confrontation combines criminal extraction, state-linked espionage, hacktivism, industrial sabotage and influence operations across transnational commercial dependencies.
en.key_risk: Treating contemporary cross-border incidents as one state-directed operation without forensics; undercounting physical, social and distributional costs of compromised supplier networks.
